page_title: MCP Explained: how the Model Context Protocol works

summary.title: MCP Explained: how the Model Context Protocol works
summary.one_liner: MCP is an open standard that lets AI apps discover and call tools, data and prompts on servers, built on JSON-RPC with defined transports, auth and capability negotiation.
takeaways: MCP has three roles: the host (AI app), the server (exposes tools, data or prompts), and the model, which decides what to use but never talks to a server directly.
A server advertises what it can do; the app shows those capabilities to the model, and when the model wants one, the app calls the server and returns the result.
MCP is not REST: it uses JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout or a single HTTP endpoint, and servers can send messages back to the client.
JSON-RPC is only the envelope; MCP defines the methods, capability negotiation, transports and auth inside it.
The page walks through every MCP message step by step, covering transports, auth, tools, sampling, tasks, tool search and codemode.
summary.summary: The page is an explainer for the Model Context Protocol, opening with a plain definition and a short glossary of hosts, servers, and the model. It contrasts MCP with REST and clarifies that JSON-RPC is only the wire format while MCP specifies methods, negotiation, transports and auth. The rest of the page, as indicated by its navigation, covers a message-flow table, the spec, tools, and interactive examples. The page text provided is short, so details of individual messages were not visible.
